newsitem.title: FRANCE: Laggard Paris bourse seen within reach of record.
newsitem.headline: Laggard Paris bourse seen within reach of record.

text.p: The Paris bourse, the laggard among the European stockmarkets, may test its two-year-old record next week, barring a catastrophe like a tumble on Wall Street, traders and analysts said on Friday.
"As long as the dollar and bonds are this strong, there's no reason to pull back," said one trader. "We could test the historic record next week."

The U.S., German and British stockmarkets have been going from record to record this year, but until recently Paris showed no sign t would attempt to surpass the historic high of 2,360.98 set by the blue chip CAC index in February 1994.

On Friday, favourable movements in the dollar and other markets and signs a 12-day truckers' strike was winding down, placed the CAC-40 within sight of its record. It closed up 25.35 points, or 1.11 percent, at 2,315.66.

The index had risen as high as 2,327.81, but Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet dampened sentiment by issuing a statement that the central bank was committed to the stability of the franc and nothing would justify a depreciation. The statement followed comments by some central bank council members questioning the franc-mark parity and urging a depreciation of the franc vis-a-vis the dollar.
